title: Introduce multi-horizon stability prober and confidence-fork canary evaluator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Add a Multi-Horizon Stability Prober to evaluate short/medium/long-term latency and throughput trends
- Add Confidence-Fork evaluator that computes Bayesian confidence across horizons and surfaces a single rollback recommendation
- Add adaptive rate limiter guard for graceful degradation when confidence indicates regression
- New dashboards and runbook guidance for canary response
description:
Context and motivation:
Redwood's current canary evaluator is good at detecting sharp regressions over a single time window but is overly sensitive to transient spikes and can miss slow drifts that only become statistically significant over longer horizons. This PR introduces two companion features: a Multi-Horizon Stability Prober that concurrently evaluates short, medium, and long horizons, and a Confidence-Fork evaluator that fuses horizon-level posterior beliefs into a single, conservative rollback signal.

What this PR changes (single continuous description):
- Add perf/canary/probers/multi_horizon_prober.py: probes that maintain three rolling windows (1m, 10m, 2h) and compute per-horizon latency/throughput posteriors using a simple Gaussian-conjugate approximation for quick updates. The prober emits horizon-tagged summary points to the evaluator stream.
- Add perf/canary/evaluator/confidence_fork.py: new evaluator that consumes horizon summaries, computes horizon-specific regression probabilities, and then applies a "confidence fork" rule: if two or more horizons exceed configurable posterior thresholds the overall canary moves to FAIL; if only the short horizon trips it opens a degraded observability path instead of failing immediately. The fork is tunable (thresholds per horizon, quorum requirement).
- Add runtime/routing/adaptive_rate_limiter.go: a lightweight rollback guard that gracefully reduces canary traffic based on the Confidence-Fork severity score rather than immediate full rollback. This is intended to allow automated, gradual traffic corking with a cooldown window.
- Telemetry: telemetry/metrics/canary_metrics.yaml adds new metrics: canary.horizon.latency_p95, canary.horizon.throughput_rate, canary.confidence.score, canary.guard.rate_reduction. Dashboards and alerts updated under console/dashboards/multi_horizon.json.
- Tests: tests/unit/test_confidence_fork.py and tests/integration/test_multi_horizon.py cover edge cases (bursty traffic, slow drift, noisy tails).
- Docs: docs/runbooks/multi_horizon_prober.md - runbook describing interpretation and recommended thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked: Linear ENG-2147
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests in CI
- [x] Dashboard and runbook updated
- [x] Backwards-compatible: evaluator registers under a feature flag (enabled for perf-canary in staging by default)

Implementation notes and rationale:
- We intentionally chose conjugate approximations for horizon posteriors to keep compute cheap; this prober runs inside the canary evaluation pipeline and must not add noticeable CPU overhead.
- The Confidence-Fork follows a conservative quorum rule (default: 2/3 horizons) to reduce noisy short-window-triggered rollbacks while still catching slow regressions.
- The adaptive rate limiter supports two modes: proportional and step. We default to proportional to preserve graceful degradation behavior and to avoid oscillations.

Testing and CI notes:
- Initial CI run failed due to a flaky integration test that relied on wall-clock timing; adjusted test harness to use simulated clock. Reran CI and all checks passed.
- Benchmarks: local perf run shows ~0.6% CPU increase on the evaluator worker at 10k rps, memory unchanged; acceptable tradeoff given improved detection fidelity.

Rollout plan:
- Merge behind feature flag and enable for perf-canary namespace in staging for 48h.
- If confidence score shows >80% false positives in staging, back off to short-horizon only mode.
- Promote to canary fleet with gradual traffic enabling and monitor canary.confidence.score and canary.guard.rate_reduction metrics.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: new metrics may increase cardinality. Mitigation: horizon tag is limited to three fixed values; metrics use low-cardinality labels.
- Risk: miscalibrated thresholds cause delayed rollbacks. Mitigation: default thresholds are conservative; runbook includes tuning guidance.

Related work: previous canary detectors (ENG-1872) and the adaptive throttler prototype (ENG-2011).
